tasks.title: Europa: Jupiter's Icy Moon
paras: Europa is the smallest of planet Jupiter’s four largest moons and the second moon out from Jupiter. Until 1979, it was just another astronomy textbook statistic. Then came the close-up images obtained by the exploratory spacecraft Voyager 2, and within days, Europa was transformed—in our perception, at least—into one of the solar system’s most intriguing worlds. The biggest initial surprise was the almost total lack of detail, especially from far away. Even at close range, the only visible features are thin, kinked brown lines resembling cracks in an egg shell. And this analogy is not far off the mark. The surface of Europa is almost pure water ice, but a nearly complete absence of craters indicates that Europa’s surface ice resembles Earth’s Antarctic ice cap. The eggshell analogy may be quite accurate since the ice could be as little as a few kilometers thick—a true shell around what is likely a subsurface liquid ocean that, in turn, encases a rocky core. The interior of Europa has been kept warm over the eons by tidal forces generated by the varying gravitational tugs of the other big moons as they wheel around Jupiter. The tides on Europa pull and relax in an endless cycle. The resulting internal heat keeps what would otherwise be ice melted almost to the surface. The cracklike marks on Europa’s icy face appear to be fractures where water or slush oozes from below.

questions.stem: The word “intriguing” in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 题型：词汇题 选项分析：intriguing意为“引起兴趣的”，对应D。 A是“改变的”。B是“完美的”。C是“可见的”。

questions.stem: The author mentions “cracks in an eggshell” in order to help readers

options.A: visualize Europa as scientists saw it in the Voyager 2 images
options.B: appreciate the extensive and detailed information available by viewing Europa from far away
options.C: understand the relationship of Europa to the solar system
options.D: recognize the similarity of Europa to Jupiter’s other moons

questions.analysis: 题型：修辞目的题 原文分析：文章提到“cracks in an eggshell”是在描述旅行者2号探测器拍摄到的欧罗巴表面特征：“Even at close range, the only visible features are thin, kinked brown lines resembling cracks in an eggshell.” 这一比喻旨在帮助读者想象欧罗巴表面的外观。对应A选项。 选项分析： B 文章明确提到从远处观察欧罗巴几乎看不到细节（“The biggest initial surprise was the almost total lack of detail, especially from far away”），因此“cracks in an eggshell”不是为了展示远距离观察的详细信息，而是描述近距离看到的裂缝特征。 C 文章中的“cracks in an eggshell”比喻仅用于描述欧罗巴表面的外观，没有涉及欧罗巴与太阳系其他部分的联系或关系。 D 文章没有比较欧罗巴与木星其他卫星的相似性，也没有用“cracks in an eggshell”来暗示这种相似性。相反，文章强调欧罗巴的独特特征（如冰面和裂缝）。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that astronomy textbooks prior to 1979

options.A: provided many contradictory statistics about Europa
options.B: considered Europa the most important of Jupiter’s moons
options.C: did not emphasize Europa because little information of interest was available
options.D: did not mention Europa because it had not yet been discovered

questions.analysis: 答案：C 解析：文章开篇提到：“文章提到在1979年之前，欧罗巴只是教科书中的统计数据，直到旅行者2号的图像揭示了其独特特征（如冰面和裂缝），才变得引人注目。这暗示1979年之前教科书没有强调欧罗巴，因为当时缺乏有趣或详细的信息，C选项符合这一推断。 A选项。文章没有提到教科书中的欧罗巴数据存在矛盾，仅说它是“another astronomy textbook statistic”，暗示数据普通且缺乏吸引力。 B选项。文章表明在1979年之前，欧罗巴只是普通的数据，没有被认为是木星最重要的卫星。相反，旅行者2号的发现才使它变得“intriguing”。 D选项。欧罗巴作为木星的卫星早在17世纪就由伽利略发现，文章提到它在1979年之前是教科书中的统计数据，说明它已被发现并记录，只是没有被特别关注。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what is the effect of Jupiter's other large moons on Europa?

options.A: They prevent Europa's subsurface waters from freezing.
options.B: They prevent tides that could damage Europa's surface.
options.C: They produce the very hard layer of ice that characterizes Europa.
options.D: They assure that the gravitational pull on Europa is maintained at a steady level.

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文分析：文章说明，木星其他大卫星的引力拉扯产生潮汐力（tidal forces），这些潮汐力使欧罗巴内部保持温暖（“keeps what would otherwise be ice melted almost to the surface”），从而防止地下水完全冻结，维持可能的地下液态海洋。A选项准确描述了这一效果。 选项分析： B 文章提到潮汐力导致欧罗巴内部加热，并未说这些卫星防止了可能破坏表面的潮汐。相反，潮汐力被认为是表面裂缝的间接原因（通过加热和水/泥浆涌出）。 C 文章描述欧罗巴表面为几乎纯水冰（“almost pure water ice”），但没有说冰层“非常坚硬”或由其他大卫星的引力直接产生。冰层特征与潮汐加热无关。 D 文章提到其他大卫星的引力是“varying gravitational tugs”（变化的引力拉扯），导致潮汐力，而不是维持稳定的引力。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what is believed to cause the cracklike marks seen on Europa’s surface?

options.A: A long period of extremely high tides
options.B: Water breaking through from beneath the surface ice
options.C: The continuous pressure of slush on top of the ice
options.D: Heat generated by the hot rocky core

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文分析：文章明确指出，表面裂缝是“fractures where water or slush oozes from below”，说明裂缝是由地下水或泥浆突破冰面造成的，B选项准确描述了这一原因。 选项分析： A 文章提到潮汐力（tides）使欧罗巴内部保持温暖，但没有说裂缝是由“极高潮汐”或“长时间极高潮汐”直接引起的。裂缝是由地下水或泥浆涌出导致的。 C 文章提到水或泥浆（slush）从冰面下方涌出（“oozes from below”），导致裂缝，而不是泥浆在冰面上施加持续压力。 D 文章提到内部热量由潮汐力产生（“tidal forces generated by the varying gravitational tugs”），而不是由“热的岩石核心”直接生成。裂缝是地下水或泥浆涌出的结果，而非核心热量直接导致。
